title: IV drip
what: Medicine or fluid flows slowly into a vein through a thin tube. A nurse or a pump controls the speed.
why: When a medicine needs to go into a vein slowly: for dehydration, antibiotics, iron, or other treatments your doctor prescribes.
duration: from 20 minutes to several hours, depending on the medicine
tell_doctor: If you have had reactions to a drip before

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come hungry, unless your doctor says otherwise.

prepare.title: Toilet
prepare.text: Use the toilet before you start. Getting up during a drip is awkward.

bring: Your phone, headphones, or a book, if the drip is long
steps: You lie down or sit in a chair
The nurse puts a thin cannula into a vein and tapes it in place
The drip with the medicine is connected and the speed is set
The nurse checks on you from time to time
When the medicine is finished, the drip is disconnected and the cannula is removed
feel: A prick when the cannula goes in
Sometimes a cool feeling in your arm from the fluid
after: Press on the spot for a few minutes
You can usually go home right away
red_flags: During the drip: itching, rash, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or swelling or pain where the cannula is. Call the nurse right away

faq.q: Can I speed up the drip myself?
faq.a: No. The nurse sets the speed. Going too fast can be dangerous.
